correctness.rationale: For finite poset incidence algebra A=I(P,F_q) with strict-interval radical J, every coefficient-linear derivation has unique cocycle-plus-inner decomposition D=δ_alpha+ad X, X∈J. Under D²=D, B=ker D surjects to A/J as a subalgebra because a−D(a) belongs B and differs from a by J. Nilpotent-ideal lifting yields complete orthogonal idempotents f_x∈B lifting E_xx; u=Σ_x f_x E_xx∈1+J conjugates them to the standard diagonal system. Thus every projection derivation is U-conjugate to δ_alpha, with unique Boolean additive cocycle alpha values 0/1. Distinct alpha remain distinct under U; stabilizer is δ_alpha(u)=0 because Z(A)∩J=0, hence orbit size q^{w(alpha)}, rank w, polynomial Σ_alpha q^{w(alpha)}T^{w(alpha)}. In char2, Boolean cocycles are Z¹ of order complex and orbit count 2^{|P|−c+β1}. Independently reproduced 4-edge crown (1+qT)^4 and histograms over q=2,3,4, including q=2 total81; the accompanying exact code checks 12 finite configurations. General proof is symbolic for all finite P, not inferred from these instances.

originality.rationale: Classical Baclawski and Krylov–Tuganbaev decompose incidence algebra derivations as inner-plus-additive cocycles, including outer classes; this structural decomposition is acknowledged. Their primary theorem does not impose composition idempotence or count radical-unit conjugacy orbits/rank polynomials. Related idempotent elements of incidence monoids are not derivations. However a general semisimple derivation or finite group-grading theorem could imply the orbit classification, and remains a best-of-knowledge priority risk.
